sentences.text: 1 0 . 2 0 0 2 r e c o r d i n g a c q u i t t a l f o r  respondent no.1 passed by the learned Judicial First Class(Municipal), Rajkot in Criminal  Case No. 796 of 1991, for the offence punishable under sections 7(i),16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention  of Food Adulteration Act 1954 ( for short 'P.F.A. Act') is assailed in this appeal under section  378 of Code of Criminal Procedure ( for short 'Cr.P.C').
R/CR.A/260/2007 JUDGMENT 2.

Having considered the rival submissions, it appears that the impugned judgement and  o r d e r w a s r e s t e d i n t e r a l i a o n b r e a c h o f  s e c t i o n 1 1 ( 1 ) ( b ) o f t h e P . F . A A c t a s a l s o o n t h e g r o u n d o f t h e a d v e r s e  inference against the appellant doubting the fact as to whether the food sample was taken in  p r e s e n c e o f p a n c h a s c o n t e m p l a t e d i n s e c t i o n  1 0 ( 7 ) o f t h e P . F . A A c t s i n c e t h e p a n c h w i t n e s s w a s n o t f o u n d w h e n h e  was sought to be summoned as witness, on the registered address.

3 . I n s o f a r a s f i r s t g r o u n d i s c o n c e r n e d , t h e r e i s n o d i s p u t e t h a t t h e  F o o d I n s p e c t o r c o l l e c t e d t h e s a m p l e s d i r e c t l y f r o m t h e c o n t a i n e r o f t h e  milk thrice; and did not divide them immediately in three equal parts as required by section

1 1 ( 1 ) ( b ) o f t h e P . F . A A c t . T h e p o w e r t o t a k e  s a m p l e s i s g i v e n t o t h e F o o d I n s p e c t o r b y s e c t i o n 1 0 ( 1 ) o f t h e P . F . A . 
Act and the procedure to be followed in this regard is contemplated in section 11 of the P.F.A. Act.

I n a c c o r d a n c e w i t h t h e l a t e r p r o v i s i o n , 
n o t i c e i s r e q u i r e d t o b e g i v e n i n w r i t i n g a t t h e t i m e o f c o l l e c t i o n o f t h e  s a m p l e o f f o o d f o r a n a l y s i s , o n t h e s p o t , d e c l a r i n g t h e i n t e n t i o n o f t h e
F o o d I n s p e c t o r t o h a v e t h e s a m p l e a n a l y z e d , t o t h e p e r s o n c o n c e r n e d

as also to other persons whose names, address and other particulars have been disclosed under  r u l e 1 4 A a n d t h e n i n a b s e n c e o f t h e  e x c e p t i o n p r o v i d e d b y t h e r u l e , t h e F o o d I n s p e c t o r i s o b l i g e d t o d i v i d e  the sample then and there into three parts and then he is required to carry out further procedure. 
4 . I n t h e i n s t a n t c a s e , t h e F o o d I n s p e c t o r d i d n o t c o l l e c t t h e s a m p l e s  into his container and then did not divide into three equal parts.

What he did was, collected the  s a m p l e s t h r i c e d i r e c t l y f r o m t h e c o n t a i n e r  b e l o n g i n g t o t h e a c c u s e d a n d s e a l e d i t i n t h r e e b o t t l e s .
T h i s i s n o t t h e  procedure contemplated in section 11(1)(b) of the P.F.A. Act.

The close R/CR.A/260/2007 JUDGMENT reading of clause (b) of subsection (1) of Section 11 would indicate that  f i r s t s a m p l e m u s t b e c o l l e c t e d a n d t h e n i t s h o u l d b e d i v i d e d i n t o t h r e e  e q u a l p a r t s . O b v i o u s p u r p o s e o f t h e p r o c e d u r e a p p e a r s t o b e t o e n s u r e  t h a t e a c h o f t h e t h r e e p a r t s r e p r e s e n t e a c h o t h e r s o t h a t e a c h p a r t c a n  b e u s e d f o r t h e p u r p o s e p r o v i d e d i n s e c t i o n 1 3 o f t h e P . F . A A c t . T h e  three samples collected directly from the container of the accused may represent  the contents of the said container but one sample would not be the representative of other in  a b s e n c e o f t h e i r s o u r c e s b e i n g

2 c o m m o n , i . e . d i v i s i o n o f o n e s a m p l e i n t o t h r e e p a r t s a n d c o n s e q u e n t l y  t h e p u r p o s e s o f t h e u s e o f t h e s a m p l e i n c l u d i n g t h o s e c o n t e m p l a t e d i n  section 13 may not be fulfilling, prejudicing the right of the accused.

The trial court has  t h e r e f o r e , r i g h t l y n o t a c c e p t e d t h e s a m p l e s t o b e t h e  r e p r e s e n t a t i v e o f e a c h o t h e r a n d h a s r i g h t l y r e c o r d e d a c q u i t t a l f o r t h e  first respondent on that count.

5 . I t h o w e v e r c o m m i t t e d s e r i o u s e r r o r i n d o u b t i n g t h e v e r y f a c t u m o f  c o l l e c t i o n o f t h e s a m p l e i n p r e s e n c e o f p a n c h a s m e r e l y o n t h e g r o u n d  t h a t a t t h a t t i m e o f s e r v i c e o f s u m m o n s , t h e p a n c h w a s n o t f o u n d a t t h e  r e g i s t e r e d a d d r e s s . O n s u c h m e r e g r o u n d , n o d o u b t a b o u t t h e d r a w i n g

o f t h e s a m p l e i n p r e s e n c e o f p a n c h a s w a s p e r m i s s i b l e i n a b s e n c e o f t h e  evidence that on the date of taking of the sample, the panch was not residing at the registered  a d d r e s s .
T h e p o s s i b i l i t y o f p a n c h h a v i n g  s h i f t e d f r o m t h e r e g i s t e r e d a d d r e s s w i t h o u t i n t i m a t i n g t o t h e c o u r t d u r i n g
the course of 10 years cannot be ruled out.

The trial court unfortunately was not mindful to this  p o s i t i o n . F u r t h e r m o r e , i t w a s i n e r r o r i n n o t  accepting the submission made by the appellant that even in absence of the evidence of panch, 
t h e c a s e c a n b e p r o v e d t h r o u g h o t h e r  evidences including that of the Food Inspector, if his testimony is found to be credible and  reliable.
It misguided itself by rejecting this R/CR.A/260/2007 JUDGMENT submission on the ground that the panch was sought to be examined but was not available.

Merely  b e c a u s e t h a t w a s s o , t h e s e t t l e d l e g a l  p o s i t i o n t h a t e v e n i n a b s e n c e o f e v i d e n c e o f p a n c h , o t h e r e v i d e n c e s  c a n b e r e l i e d u p o n d i d n o t g e t i n f l u e n c e d .
T h e f a c t r e m a i n s t h a t t h e r e  w a s s u c h o t h e r e v i d e n c e o n r e c o r d a n d t h e c o u r t b e l o w w a s u n d e r t h e
obligation to appreciate the same.

6 . H o w e v e r i n v i e w o f b r e a c h o f s e c t i o n 1 1 ( 1 ) ( b ) o f t h e P . F . A A c t , 
t h i s C o u r t i s n o t i n c l i n e d t o i n t e r f e r e i n t h e o r d e r o f a c q u i t t a l .
T h e a p p e a l  therefore must fail and is accordingly ordered to be dismissed.
7. Record and Proceedings if any shall be returned to the Court below.
